title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Deepfake technology was used to create non-consensual sexual imagery of Dutch public figures. The manipulated videos placed real faces onto pornographic footage and were hosted on a platform with millions of monthly visitors. The system was deployed without apparent safeguards to prevent this abuse or to remove such material once posted.

This is a failure of content moderation at scale. The platform allowed creation and distribution of non-consensual intimate imagery, which is illegal in the Netherlands. Catching this would have required either automated detection of deepfake pornography or human review processes triggered by reports from victims and the public.

It is not established whether the platform knew the material was present, why detection systems failed if they existed, or what measures the hosting company took after becoming aware of the problem.

summary:
Multiple well-known Dutch women are considering legal action after their faces appeared in fake pornographic videos on an online platform that receives 13 million monthly visitors. The manipulated content features Dutch entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government officials, mayors, and members of the Royal Family. Several victims and their representatives have confirmed they have filed reports or are exploring legal options. The videos are created by digitally placing a celebrity's head onto pornographic footage. Deputy Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and encouraged victims to report them.

Deepfake pornography falls under revenge porn laws and is therefore criminal in the Netherlands. Legal experts advise victims to file complaints with police, who can then attempt to shut down websites hosting the material. Other options include starting group lawsuits, filing complaints with the data protection authority, or contacting hosting companies. An earlier case resulted in a 39-year-old man from Amersfoort receiving a conditional sentence of 180 hours for creating fake videos of television presenter Welmoed Sijtsma. Legal experts warn that without government intervention, more fake pornographic videos featuring celebrities will likely emerge.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
